symptoms: Many small round spots, about 2 to 3 mm, with grey centres and dark edges
Tiny black dots (fruiting bodies) visible inside the spots
Spots start on lower leaves after fruit set and move upward
Leaves yellow, wither and drop, fruit itself usually stays clean

severity_cues.early: Scattered small spots on lower leaves only
severity_cues.advanced: Hundreds of spots per leaf, heavy defoliation, exposed fruit at sunscald risk

favorable_conditions: Warm (20 to 25 C) and humid weather, long leaf-wetness periods, splashing rain

treatment.summary: Protect new growth with scheduled fungicide sprays and reduce leaf wetness
steps: Remove badly infected lower leaves and destroy them off the field
Spray Chlorothalonil 75 WP at 2.0 g per litre, repeat every 7 days
Mulch to stop rain splashing spores from soil onto leaves
Water at the base, never on the leaves, and in the morning only

products.name: Chlorothalonil 75 WP
products.label_source: CIB&RC registered label, waiting period 7 days

products.name: Mancozeb 75 WG
products.label_source: CIB&RC registered label, waiting period 7 days

organic: Copper oxychloride 50 WP at 2.5 g per litre
Staking and pruning for airflow, two-year rotation out of tomato

source.org: TNAU Agritech Portal, crop protection, tomato diseases
source.title: Tomato: Septoria leaf spot management

safety_notes: Wear gloves, mask and full sleeves while spraying
Do not harvest within 7 days of any fungicide spray
